bull.b: De novo/moderate-risk framing, Breakthrough Device status and active CMS/RAPID and CPT engagement create durable commercial advantages. If clinical results hold, these regulatory and reimbursement pathways materially improve the odds of timely coverage and hospital adoption, lowering long-term access barriers.

bull.t: Pivotal trial execution and data robustness
bull.b: A large, well-run sham-controlled pivotal with high retention and predefined co-primary endpoints strengthens evidentiary credibility and regulatory confidence. Durable impact: strong trial execution reduces approval and commercialization execution risk and supports uptake if results confirm benefit.

Progressing RJVA-001 into first-in-human studies diversifies the pipeline beyond a single procedural product and creates a longer-term value driver. Durable implications include potential partnership interest, milestone funding options, and a differentiated therapeutic franchise if early signals validate the approach.

bear.t: Limited cash runway and financing risk
bear.b: With liquidity only into early 2027 and management deferring capital raises until pivotal readouts, the company faces a persistent financing cliff. Any delays, adverse results, or reimbursement setbacks could force dilutive financing or program delays, materially constraining long-term execution options.

bear.t: High cash burn and negative operating cash flow
bear.b: Sustained, large negative cash flows indicate heavy investment without commercial revenue. Persistent burn will deplete reserves absent successful financing or revenue, reducing strategic flexibility and increasing the likelihood of resource-driven reprioritization or program delays over the medium term.

bear.t: Elevated leverage and historical balance-sheet stress
bear.b: Material leverage relative to a small equity base raises refinancing and solvency risk for a pre-revenue biotech.
